rows.answer:
You need sign-off from the **change approver of the team that owns the affected service**, which for archived event payloads is the Driftwood service. Changing these lifecycle rules is a normal change under the production change approval policy [1][2]. The policy doesn't name the approver. Look up the owning team and its approver in the service catalog and engineering team directory [1].

If Driftwood stores Restricted data, you also need sign-off from the **Head of Security** or the security on-call delegate. Restricted services are marked in the service catalog [1]. Archived event payloads are customer data [2], so check that marking.

Other requirements that apply:

- **ADR:** Any change that alters how long customer data is kept needs an ADR, linked from the PR [1].
- **Customer notice:** Shortening retention needs a 30-day customer notice from the account team for Enterprise contracts that reference a retention period [1].
- **Process:** Add the `change:normal` label to the PR, fill in the risk and rollback sections, and request review from the approver as a CODEOWNERS reviewer. Approvals are valid for 7 days [1].
- **Freezes:** The holiday freeze runs December 18, 2026 to January 4, 2027, and normal changes are blocked then [1].
- **Retention limits:** Under retention standard v2, the default archive period is 365 days. Enterprise customers can contract for up to 730 days with security team approval [2]. Any retention beyond 400 days without security approval is not allowed for sales to offer [4].

A change to when reminder texts go out is a **significant change**, so it needs three approvals, not just one:

1. **System steward approval.** The steward for the team that owns the system. Halcyon's policy lists Felix Brandt (Digital Health Engineering, Patient Engagement) as steward for patient-facing reminders, but the sources don't say which team owns this specific reminder system, so confirm that first [2].
2. **Clinical safety sign-off** from the CMIO, Dr. Anjali Rao, or her delegate, Associate CMIO Dr. Benedict Osei [2]. Dr. Osei has already withheld sign-off on a different item this month, so expect scrutiny of patient-facing wording [3].
3. **Review at the Clinical Systems Change Advisory Board (CSCAB)**, which meets Wednesdays at 14:00 Eastern [2]. The next meeting is Wednesday, November 4, 2026, if you can get on the agenda in time.

If the change also moves the reminder job to a different runner or server, it is a cutover. That requires a written runbook that explains how double-sending is prevented [2]. This rule came from incident IR-0412, when a runner cutover caused patients to receive reminders two to four times [1].

You need sign-off from **PLAT's change approver**. Hydrant is owned by PLAT, and its configuration, including each cell's floor and ceiling, lives in the PLAT infrastructure repo. Raising a ceiling counts as a normal change under the production change approval policy [1][6]. Security sign-off isn't needed because Hydrant stores no customer data and isn't a Restricted service [1].

To make the change:
- Add the `change:normal` label to the PR and fill in the risk and rollback sections [6].
- Request review from the PLAT change approver (or delegate) as a CODEOWNERS reviewer [6].
- Approvals are valid for 7 days, so re-request if the change hasn't shipped by then [6].

For context, us-east's current Hydrant floor and ceiling are 16 and 64 gateway replicas, and it had 6,240 workspaces on October 1 [2]. Hydrant pages the Data Plane primary on-call when a cell sits at its ceiling for 10 minutes, because that usually points to a gateway problem rather than real traffic [1]. Before raising the ceiling, it's worth checking whether the gateways are misbehaving. If you only need to pin a replica count temporarily, a hold (up to 4 hours) is a standard change and needs no approval [1].

A Growth-plan customer (the $1,200/month plan) can send **50 requests per second** to `POST /v2/events/batch` [1][2]. Each request can carry up to **10,000 events or 10 MB**, whichever is hit first [1].

Other limits that apply:

- **Scope:** limits are per workspace, not per API key, so all keys in the workspace share the 50 req/s budget [1].
- **Bursts:** short bursts up to 2x the limit (100 req/s) are allowed for 10 seconds [1].
- **Over the limit:** the API returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header. The SDKs back off automatically [1].
- **Quota:** rejected requests don't count against the monthly event quota [1].
- **Temporary raise:** for a one-off backfill, the Data Plane on-call primary can grant a temporary raise of up to 72 hours [1]. The internal doc doesn't say how large that raise can be, so the customer would need to request it.

The plan's included volume is 100 million events per month, with overage at $8 per additional million [2].

**Keep trying for 30 minutes. If you still can't reach the ordering clinician, the result goes to the on-call medical director.** The clinical escalation protocol requires that critical results reach the ordering clinician within 60 minutes, and if that clinician can't be reached in 30 minutes, the result goes to the medical director on call [1]. The protocol doesn't describe a longer retry period, so don't wait beyond that 30-minute mark.

To reach the on-call medical director, call the Halcyon answering service at 555-0144 and choose option 2. The service pages the on-call director and pages the backup if there's no callback within 10 minutes [2]. Don't text physicians' personal mobile numbers, because pages through the answering service are logged and timed [2].

Document every critical result notification in the chart with the time and the person notified [1].

Riverbend should be scheduling **1.5 medical assistants per clinician**. Riverbend is in the Medium band, which uses that ratio under the current standard [1].

- **Why Medium:** Riverbend averaged 46 visits a day in Q3 2026 [3]. The current standard puts 40 to 80 visits a day in the Medium band [1].
- **Rounding:** The standard says to round up to the next whole person [1]. In practice, one physician or NP seeing patients would mean 2 MAs scheduled. That is my reading of the rounding rule, so confirm it with Clinical Operations if it matters for a specific schedule.
- **Superseded standard:** The 2025 standard listed Medium at 1.25 MAs per clinician, but it was replaced effective September 1, 2026 [1][2].

The current standard also requires Medium clinics to have at least 2 physicians or NPs on site, 1 RN on site, and 3 front desk staff [1].

The expired AED is **AED-ELH-01 at ELH (Elmhurst)**. Its pads expired on September 30, 2026 [1]. The unit is marked "Action needed," with replacement pads ordered on October 9 and due by November 6 [1]. In the meantime, a spare pad set borrowed from ELP is in use [1].

The clinic manager is responsible for closing the fix. Site clinic managers must close "Action needed" items, record the fix in the equipment log, and tell Clinical Operations [1]. Patrick Oduya took over as manager at Elmhurst on September 14, 2026 [2]. The sources don't name the ELH code explicitly, but the directory lists Elmhurst and the inventory lists ELH, so I've treated them as the same site.

Until the new pads arrive, the unit is still in use with the borrowed set. The sources don't say whether that's acceptable. Also, the borrowed set is an A3 set, and pads must not be swapped between A3 and A5 models [1].

Only **Northgate** will be open at 1 p.m. on a Saturday. The Juniper pilot runs at Riverside, Elm Park and Northgate [1].

- **Riverside:** Saturday hours are 08:00–12:00, so it closes before 1 p.m. [2]
- **Elm Park:** Saturday hours are 09:00–12:00, so it closes before 1 p.m. [2]
- **Northgate:** Saturday hours are 08:00–14:00, extended from September 5, 2026, so it is open at 1 p.m. [2]

The pilot doesn't start until January 12, 2027 [1]. These hours are from the October 12, 2026 directory, so check for later changes.
